- Initiate empiric antibiotic therapy for presumed UTI (Trimethoprim, one tablet twice daily for 3 days).
- Advise over-the-counter Paracetamol as needed for pain.
- Increase oral fluids; consider cranberry juice.
- Recommend pregnancy test to rule out early pregnancy/complication due to ongoing risk (on Implanon, but not absolutely excluded).
- Return to clinic or seek further care if symptoms worsen or do not improve within a few days.

1. Urinary tract infection (cystitis) – High likelihood.  
   - Classic presentation: lower abdominal pain, increased urinary frequency, pink urine, mild systemic symptoms (hot/sweaty), mild nausea. No severe pyelonephritis features.
2. Pelvic inflammatory disease (PID) – Moderate likelihood.  
   - Sexually active female with lower abdominal pain and recent intercourse; lacks classical PID features (no discharge, cervical motion tenderness, or documented fever); urinary symptoms more prominent.
